answer: A tool sharpening log is stamped at the tool bench with the tool name, the stone grade, and the edge test. The inlet is the quiet part of the proof. A farm would have to sharpen 900 real tools at 900 real benches, while one binder sharpens a single set. A stranger cannot borrow the jetty that belongs to the keeper. An economy that checks such records leaves a basalt of room for copies.
